title: ResMed Mask Leak Warning
shortDescription: Machine detects unintentional leak above acceptable threshold.
fullDescription:
ResMed AirSense and AirCurve devices track leak rate in liters per minute. A 'High Leak' warning appears when leak exceeds the machine's threshold for a sustained period. Causes include worn cushion, incorrect mask size, or mouth leak on nasal users.

Address leaks promptly - excessive leak reduces therapy effectiveness and wakes other sleepers.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cushion
fixSteps.instruction: Check cushion for tears, distortion, or buildup. Replace monthly per guidelines.

fixSteps.title: Run mask fit test
fixSteps.instruction: Use the Mask Fit feature in My Options to verify seal.

fixSteps.title: Adjust headgear
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten headgear evenly - not too tight or it distorts the seal.

whenToCallPro: Consult your sleep technician or supplier if leaks persist after new cushion and proper fitting - you may need a different mask style.

faq.a: Monthly for nasal/pillow cushions, every 3 months for full-face.

title: ResMed High Leak Detected in Therapy Data
shortDescription: myAir or clinician report shows high leak percentage.
fullDescription: High leak score in therapy reports means leaks exceeded threshold for a large portion of the night. This reduces the score shown in the myAir app. Review mask condition, strap fit, and whether you sleep with your mouth open on a nasal mask.

fixSteps.title: Review myAir trends
fixSteps.instruction: Check if leaks correlate with sleep position changes.

fixSteps.title: Try chin strap
fixSteps.instruction: If mouth leak is suspected, try a chin strap or full-face mask.

whenToCallPro: Speak with your sleep physician or DME if leaks remain high despite mask changes - pressure or mask type may need adjustment.
videoSearchQuery: ResMed myAir high leak score fix

faq.a: Yes, significant leak can lower effective pressure and reduce therapy benefit.

title: ResMed Blower Motor Fault
fullDescription:
The blower motor generates the therapy pressure. A blower fault indicates the machine cannot reach or regulate the prescribed pressure. This is a hardware issue requiring manufacturer service - do not open the device.

Stop using the machine and contact your DME or ResMed support.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and restart to rule out transient fault.

fixSteps.title: Contact DME
fixSteps.instruction: If fault returns, contact your home medical equipment supplier immediately.

whenToCallPro: Always - blower faults are medical device hardware issues. Do not attempt internal repair. Contact your DME, ResMed, or healthcare provider.

faq.a: Yes, ask your DME about a loaner unit while yours is serviced.

title: ResMed Humidifier Error
shortDescription: Machine cannot detect or heat the humidifier tub.
fullDescription: The HumidAir tub must be fully seated and have water for the humidifier to operate. This error can also indicate corroded contacts from mineral buildup or a failed heater plate.

fixSteps.title: Reseat tub
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and firmly reinsert the water tub until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe pins on back of tub and in machine well with dry cloth.

whenToCallPro: Contact DME if error persists after cleaning and reseating - heater plate may have failed.

faq.a: Yes - tap water leaves mineral deposits that can damage the unit.

title: ResMed Heated Tube Error
shortDescription: Machine cannot detect ClimateLineAir heated tube.
fullDescription: The heated tube has a sensor wire that communicates with the machine. When the tube is standard (non-heated) or has a broken sensor, the tube error appears. Verify you are using the correct tube type or replace a damaged heated tube.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tube
fixSteps.instruction: Look for kinks or crushed sections near the cuffs.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Firmly push the tube cuff onto the machine outlet.

fixSteps.title: Replace tube
fixSteps.instruction: Order a new ClimateLineAir tube if damaged.

whenToCallPro: If replacement tube still errors, contact DME.

faq.a: Standard tubes work but not heated features. Use ResMed ClimateLineAir for heated function.

title: ResMed SD Card Error
shortDescription: Machine cannot read or write therapy data to SD card.
fullDescription: ResMed uses SD cards to log therapy data for clinician review. A card error means the card is missing, locked, corrupt, or damaged. Therapy still runs without a card but no data is recorded locally.

causes.cause: Card lock switch in LOCK position

fixSteps.title: Reinsert card
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinsert the SD card in the side slot.

fixSteps.title: Check lock switch
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure tiny lock slider on card edge is in the unlocked position.

fixSteps.title: Replace card
fixSteps.instruction: Use a 2-32 GB FAT32 SD card or one from your DME.

whenToCallPro: Your DME may require their specific SD card format - call if error persists.

faq.a: Yes, airflow therapy continues but data is not saved to card.

title: ResMed Data Transfer Failed to myAir
shortDescription: Machine cannot upload therapy data via cellular or Wi-Fi.
fullDescription: AirSense 10 uses built-in cellular, AirSense 11 uses Wi-Fi and cellular. Transfer failures usually result from poor signal where the machine sits. Moving the machine to a window-facing location often resolves it.

fixSteps.title: Move machine
fixSteps.instruction: Place machine closer to a window for better signal.

fixSteps.title: Reconfigure Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: On AirSense 11, re-enter Wi-Fi in My Options > Network.

whenToCallPro: Contact DME if signal is strong but data still fails to upload.

faq.a: ResMed includes cellular at no charge for covered devices.

title: ResMed Low Battery Warning (Mobile Power)
shortDescription: External battery (ResMed Power Station II or equivalent) low.
fullDescription: When using a battery pack for travel, ResMed displays a low battery warning when voltage drops below the therapy threshold. Most CPAP batteries last 8-14 hours depending on pressure and humidifier use.

fixSteps.title: Disable humidifier
fixSteps.instruction: On battery, turn off heated humidifier to nearly double runtime.

whenToCallPro: Contact DME if battery no longer holds a charge.

faq.a: Yes, most CPAP batteries are TSA-approved under 160 Wh in carry-on.

title: ResMed Mask Fit Issues and Discomfort
shortDescription: Mask causes pressure sores, leaks, or discomfort.
fullDescription: Proper mask fit is the biggest factor in therapy comfort and adherence. If the mask leaves deep marks, causes sores, or leaks despite tightening, the size or style may be wrong. Work with your supplier to try alternative sizes or styles.

causes.cause: Mask style doesn't fit face shape

fixSteps.title: Measure face
fixSteps.instruction: Use ResMed's online fit guide or visit DME for a professional fitting.

fixSteps.title: Try mask liner
fixSteps.instruction: A cloth liner can reduce skin irritation.

whenToCallPro: See your sleep physician or DME for alternative masks - insurance often covers replacement.

faq.a: Cushions monthly, frames every 3 months, full mask annually.

title: ResMed Pressure Feels Too High
shortDescription: User reports uncomfortable pressure during therapy.
fullDescription: Some users find the prescribed pressure uncomfortable, especially at start. Use EPR (Expiratory Pressure Relief) or the Ramp feature to ease into therapy. Never change prescribed pressure without physician approval.

fixSteps.title: Enable Ramp
fixSteps.instruction: My Options > Ramp Time > choose 15-45 min so pressure starts low.

fixSteps.title: Adjust EPR
fixSteps.instruction: My Options > EPR - can be set to 1, 2, or 3 cmH2O lower on exhale.

whenToCallPro: Consult your sleep physician before changing prescribed pressure settings. Do not self-adjust pressure - this is a medical setting.

faq.a: Only with physician direction. EPR and Ramp are patient-adjustable comfort features.

title: ResMed Pressure Feels Too Low
shortDescription: User reports pressure not sufficient, may feel suffocating.
fullDescription: If you still feel apneas or air hunger, the prescribed pressure may be too low or the mask may be leaking. Do not self-adjust the prescription - contact your sleep physician or DME.

fixSteps.title: Check leak
fixSteps.instruction: Review myAir leak score - fix leak first.

fixSteps.title: Contact physician
fixSteps.instruction: Request pressure titration review with your sleep doctor.

whenToCallPro: Always consult your sleep physician. Low pressure that leaves apnea untreated is a health risk - do not delay.

faq.a: No - prescribed pressure requires a clinician. Ask for a retitration.

title: myAir Reports Not Enough Usage Data
shortDescription: myAir cannot score a night because usage is under threshold.
fullDescription: myAir requires a minimum of 1 hour use per night to score. Nights under that are marked 'Not Enough Data'. Use the machine longer or contact DME about adherence concerns.

fixSteps.title: Wear longer
fixSteps.instruction: Aim for 4+ hours of wear per night.

fixSteps.title: Address discomfort
fixSteps.instruction: If taking mask off early, troubleshoot fit.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot tolerate therapy, contact your sleep physician - untreated apnea has serious health consequences.

faq.a: Medicare and most insurers require 4+ hours for 22 of 30 nights for compliance.

title: ResMed Firmware Update Required
shortDescription: Machine prompts for a firmware update.
fullDescription: AirSense 11 can receive over-the-air firmware updates. When prompted, allow the update to complete - it typically takes 5-15 minutes. Do not unplug during the update.

fixSteps.title: Accept update
fixSteps.instruction: Tap Accept and leave machine plugged in.

fixSteps.title: Wait for restart
fixSteps.instruction: Machine reboots automatically - do not interrupt power.

whenToCallPro: Call DME if the update fails mid-way and machine won't boot.

faq.a: No, updates preserve your prescribed settings.

title: ResMed Air Filter Replacement Due
shortDescription: Filter is dirty or has reached replacement interval.
fullDescription: ResMed CPAPs use a hypoallergenic air filter at the rear inlet. Replace monthly or when visibly gray. A dirty filter reduces airflow and can trigger pressure issues.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Slide out old filter at rear inlet, insert new hypoallergenic filter.

whenToCallPro: DIY - filters are a user-replaceable consumable.

faq.a: Standard filters are disposable - do not wash. Some reusable foam filters can be rinsed.

title: ResMed Rainout - Water in Tube
shortDescription: Condensation forms in tube and sprays on face.
fullDescription: Rainout happens when the humidifier output is warmer than room air and moisture condenses in the tube. Use ClimateLineAir heated tubing with Auto climate control, or lower humidity level in cold rooms.

fixSteps.title: Lower humidity
fixSteps.instruction: My Options > Humidity Level, reduce by 1 step.

fixSteps.title: Use tube cover
fixSteps.instruction: Insulate tube with a fleece cover.

fixSteps.title: Upgrade to heated tube
fixSteps.instruction: Install ClimateLineAir heated tube for auto climate.

faq.a: Not usually, but large amounts of water can interfere with therapy and cause coughing.

title: Error E33
fullDescription: Pressure sensor fault. Common diagnostic on ResMed cpap. Resolve by following manufacturer service procedure.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Clean charging contacts or ports with soft cloth.

whenToCallPro: If reset/charge doesn't fix, contact warranty service.

faq.a: Most personal care devices have 1-2 year warranty.
Cleaning and reset usually fix common issues.
